verdict.rationale: Turso's first-party vector search guide says vector search is a native feature with no extensions required. Embeddings are stored alongside relational data and queried with built-in distance functions, so no separate vector database is needed. A community user and a Turso employee corroborate the native support, and the AI-memory guide shows it in use. Missing for 10: hands-on independent confirmation of running similarity queries (the community mention is speculative), evidence of indexing or ANN performance at scale, and deeper documentation (one user called the vector docs not robust).

support.subject: As a developer, I can store embeddings and run vector similarity search natively without adding a separate vector database

citations.quote: Turso supports vector search as a native feature — no extensions required. Store vector embeddings alongside your relational data and query them using built-in distance functions for similarity search.
A persistent memory system lets agents store lessons and retrieve relevant context via vector search.
It natively supports vector embeddings, which seems like it could be nice.
It adds new features on top of SQLite, such as vector search, replication, server mode, and more.
